notes.page_statement: The letter proposes studying sheaves, complexes and fields/champs constructible for a fixed partition, or locally constant on each part. It asks for stability under usual operations, including derived Hom and Rj_*j^*. It states stability of constructible torsion sheaves in the excellent/resolution setting, with the residual-characteristic qualification, but distinguishes that claim from stability for one fixed partition. It says stricter equisingularity conditions are needed and expresses an expectation that sufficiently fine suitable stratifications will be obtainable. It begins an example at the foot.
author_explicit_uncertainty: Je pense néanmoins qu’un raffinement des techniques connues montrera que X admet des stratifications arbitrairement fines
notes.author_uncertainty_comment: The expectation is introduced by Je pense néanmoins and future montrera. The opening of raffinement is visually uncertain in this reading, independently of that authorial qualification.
notes.page_date_title_evidence: Observed author number 28 at top centre; archive pencil 173 at bottom-left. No date, title, salutation or signature occurs on this page. The text starts and ends as a continuation.

There is no separate diagram, display or independent separator stroke. Ordinary dashes at L9 and L15 and the line-end hyphens in partition and raffinement are accounted for as text. Fixée and Hom each have one underline.

The distinct point after constructibles is transcribed literally; its presence is not treated as proof of a sentence boundary.
notes.bottom_edge: Broken/doubled contours at the foot affect the whole final line. They are not by themselves evidence that pour is cancelled. Pour and présent remain doubtful; notre and propos are supported by their surviving letter forms.
notes.paragraphing: The main text has continuous spacing. Changes of sentence or subject alone were not made into paragraph breaks.

workflow_feedback: The one-crop-per-open-place rule worked for this page. A small phrase crop at the damaged foot was necessary to compare word boundaries, while individual doubt statuses are still recorded separately.

Clarify an encoding convention for cancelled words that occupy a second baseline below intact live text without a caret: the physical attachment can be recorded reliably, but linear TeX ordering necessarily chooses an anchor.
The brief correctly distinguishes visible-point presence from its role; this was useful for both the literal point after constructibles and the second tiny dab before En fait.
